newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Robbers end Russian orchestra's tour on flat note.
newsitem.headline: Robbers end Russian orchestra's tour on flat note.

text.p: A triumphant tour of Japan by the St Petersburg Philharmonic, one of Russia's leading orchestras, ended on a sour note when armed highway robbers held up the musicians' bus after their flight home.

Five men armed with a Kalashnikov assault rifle burst on to the coach after an accomplice, who had inveigled his way into the party at the airport, brought it to a stop on a dark and lonely stretch of highway outside the city by feigning illness.
A police spokesman told Reuters the bandits forced the musicians to hand over money and valuables worth about $30,000 in the raid on November 5. They had no leads on the culprits yet.

Like the rest of Russia's cultural elite, the Philharmonic, which bears the name of Shostakovich, has severe cash problems. Only about a third of government subsidies have been paid and musicians count on foreign tours for a big part of their income.
